beats.text: What makes a life good? Aristotle's answer wasn't pleasure, or money, or fame.
It was eudaimonia — flourishing. Not a feeling you chase, but a life done well, over time.
And you reach it, he said, through virtue — which always sits between two extremes.
Courage is the mean between cowardice and recklessness. Generosity, between stinginess and waste.
Too little and too much are both failures. The good life is a matter of the right amount.
And virtue is a habit, not a mood. You become brave by doing brave things, again and again.
We are what we repeatedly do. So excellence is not an act, but a habit.

source_note: Ideas from the Nicomachean Ethics (public-domain translation) — paraphrased.
